title: GSA opens agentic-AI OneGov deal with CORAS at 40–80% discount through September 2027
subtitle: Federal agencies get FedRAMP-High access to CORAS' GARY digital workforce for governed automation of back-office work, with a 90-day pilot up front.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: The General Services Administration on July 28 added CORAS.ai to its OneGov IT modernization program, letting federal agencies buy CORAS' GARY agentic-AI digital workforce at steep discounts through September 20, 2027. GARY Execute is discounted 40%; GARY Insight is discounted 80%. The offer includes a 90-day pilot. CORAS is delivered through a FedRAMP High / IL5 / IL6++ platform already authorized for use at the Department of Defense.

GARY is not a chatbot. CORAS describes it as a governed digital workforce that sits in front of existing mission data and enterprise systems and executes back-office work — analysis, reporting, workflow steps — under human-authored rules, with an approval gate on every result and a full audit trail. The design point is that the automation runs on top of tools agencies already use, not as a rip-and-replace, and every completed action is signed off by a person before it counts.

The OneGov structure is doing real work here. Rather than each of ~440 federal agencies negotiating its own agentic-AI contract, GSA is centralizing the terms and applying a governmentwide discount schedule that runs 14 months. The pattern echoes recent OneGov deals for cloud, cybersecurity, and productivity software: the government treats a category as strategic, then negotiates once for everyone. That gives agencies without a sophisticated AI procurement team a compliant on-ramp to agents — which is most of them.

For learners and early-career engineers: this is how agentic AI actually enters an enterprise. It arrives through a procurement schedule with a FedRAMP boundary, an audit trail, and human approvals — not as an autonomous coworker. If you want to build for government, or for any regulated industry, the parts of the stack that get you deployed are the governance and evidence layers, not the model. Learn what an audit trail and an approval-gated workflow look like, because that is the shape of AI work you will ship into these environments.
